items.headline: 'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat
items.blurb: Some Republicans tell the BBC the president's focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost them.
items.text: Inside the Republican Party, initial shock at the stunning election results on Tuesday night quickly gave way to anger with US President Donald Trump. After Democrats won upset after upset in deep-red states like Texas, Kansas and South Carolina, some Republicans focused their ire on Trump, arguing that his focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost the party control of Congress. "It's on him. It's not on anybody else. It's a total, complete rejection of President Trump," Bill Miller, a top Republican lobbyist in Texas, told the BBC. "This is a disaster of the first magnitude. Nobody saw it coming like this." Most Republicans expected to lose control of the House and were clear-eyed about the challenge of holding onto the Senate in a tough election cycle that favoured the party out of power. But some said in interviews that Trump dragged them down with unpopular policies, a low job approval rating and obsession over construction projects in Washington. items.headline: British healthcare worker with Ebola evacuated from DR Congo to UK
items.blurb: Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed.
items.text: Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed. “A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola ,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday. “The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.” The patient, whose identity is unknown, is in a stable condition and is expected to arrive in the UK on Wednesday or Thursday before being transferred in a specialist ambulance to a “high consequence” infectious disease unit, according to an official document seen by Reuters. A humanitarian organisation sent the worker to DR Congo to help in the response to the outbreak, which is the second largest on record. items.headline: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief
items.blurb: With Canada-US trade talks back on, Tuesday’s midterm Democratic wave puts pressure on the White House to come to a deal.
items.text: It was the midterm result that many in Canada had hoped for - a Democratic sweep that was in part a repudiation by American voters of Donald Trump's tariff on close trade allies. "I was doing cartwheels down the street," said Ontario Premier Doug Ford on Wednesday morning, calling it "a victory for Canada". Tuesday night's result is unlikely to grant Canada relief from those tariffs any time soon, but there is anticipation that the political shifts could create a more favourable environment for Ottawa to get the best deal now that on-again-off-again trade talks are back on. US voters cited affordability as a main concern heading into the midterms and a survey by the Cato Institute in September , external suggested that about 75% believe the tariffs have raised prices. In states like Maine and Michigan, tariffs played a significant role in the hard-fought races. In Maine, incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins clashed with the White House over tariffs. items.blurb: Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling…
items.text: Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure. The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party. However, polls showed it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the last municipal elections in 2021 and 40.2% in 2024’s national elections . In Kensington, a diverse Johannesburg suburb that has sustained repeated water and power outages in recent weeks, voters said they wanted to see change. The city is currently led by Dada Morero, the ANC mayor, in coalition with the far-left Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) and the rightwing populist Patriotic Alliance (PA). “Service delivery is bad, it’s horrible,” said Tshepiso Makotse, 26, a call centre worker. “Water,

items.headline: Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing
items.blurb: At least 40 people were killed and another 30 may still be under the rubble after Monday's attack on a Ukrainian village, Kyiv says.
items.text: A bodycam video has been released by Ukraine police which they say shows the moments between two powerful Russian bomb strikes that killed at least 40 people at an aid centre and a shelter. The footage, from a camera on one of the killed police officers, shows residents of the southern village of Kamyshuvakha going to an underground shelter after the first attack on Monday. Soon after a blast is heard and flames are seen as the shelter is hit. President Volodymyr Zelensky said more than 30 people may still be under the rubble, as a search operation continued for the third day. Nine gliding bombs, some weighing 3,000kg, hit the village as people had gathered to get humanitarian aid, Ukraine said. It shows huge devastation after the first bomb strike on the village in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, as shocked local residents stare at the rubble. items.headline: Democrats won Congress. But can they deliver on their promises?
items.blurb: Despite their midterm election victories, Democrats face major obstacles to reining in Trump on Iran, tariffs and more.
items.text: Democrats rode a blue wave to victory in the United States midterm elections , winning control of both chambers of Congress . Now comes the question of whether they can deliver on their promises. The party campaigned on bringing down the cost of living, ending the war on Iran and holding President Donald Trump accountable, as well as pushing back against his immigration crackdown. But Democrats won’t take control of Congress until January. Even then, there’s only so much they’ll be able to do without Republican cooperation. Most bills need 60 votes to get past a filibuster in the Senate, and even if Democrats manage that, Trump can still veto their legislation. He has already threatened to do just that, telling a podcast on Monday, “I’ll veto everything.” But the Democrats now also have other tools at their disposal, including power over Senate confirmations and control over committees that can launch investigations. items.text: There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective C ora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area. In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa , meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare). Soon, they were taking water for their panning and processing from the organisation’s two 25,000-litre water tanks, which are filled irregularly by the city government for the 100 or so rescued and injured animals on site. “We’ve asked them really nicely and haven’t ever refused them water to drink … But, for the first time ever, we closed the gate at 12 midday, because we literally had about two buckets of water

items.headline: French blood storage impacted by freezer hacks as theories swirl about culprits
items.blurb: The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said cold rooms storing blood were impacted by hackers.
items.text: French authorities say that fridges used in medical facilities to store blood for donations were impacted by recent cyber-attacks by unknown hackers. The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said cold rooms storing blood were impacted by hackers, with temperatures set to rise - but staff intervened to protect blood supplies. "No health impact has been identified and no loss of blood products is to be reported," the EFS said. Up until now, only supermarkets were known to have been impacted by the hacks. Meanwhile rumours have been circulating online about Russian hacktivist groups claiming they worked together to hack one of the systems that was used in the attacks which have affected European supermarkets. Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance posted that they successfully hacked Danfoss which led to speculation that they were the culprits behind the freezer hacks. But analysts now question whether or not that meant they were behind the supermarket cyber-attacks. While Russian groups are not being ruled out, experts say Iranian hacktivists or nation state hackers - or even teenagers pulling pranks - could also be the culprits. Cyber-security

items.headline: Mahadev app co-promoter Ravi Uppal arrested in UAE, India moves for his extradition
items.blurb: Authorities in Dubai arrested a 46-year-old Ravi Uppal based on an Interpol Red Notice issued by Indian probe agencies, officials told PTI
items.text: Ravi Uppal, co-promoter of the multi-crore Mahadev online betting app, has been arrested in the UAE, and India is moving to extradite him, officials said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026). The development follows the return from Oman on November 1 of Mr. Uppal's friend and another Mahadev app promoter, Saurabh Chandrakar, after a court there allowed his extradition to India in a money-laundering case being probed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). Authorities in Dubai arrested a 46-year-old Uppal based on an Interpol Red Notice issued by Indian probe agencies, officials told PTI . The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the ED are working to extradite him to India, they said. Ravi Uppal was once detained by authorities in the UAE in 2023, but agencies later found that he was in Australia. Probe agencies have claimed that Mr. Uppal obtained a passport from Vanuatu, an archipelagic country located in the South Pacific Ocean, just like Chandrakar. It charged Mr. Uppal in October 2023, stating that he "generated and enjoyed proceeds of crime and is involved in their concealment and layering".

items.headline: Digital traffic simulation model, road safety audit for 2,205km of Delhi roads
items.blurb: Traffic congestion in Delhi has been increasing, with even stretches that earlier experienced smooth traffic movement now witnessing frequent bottlenecks
items.text: Under spotlight for congestion on Delhi’s arterial road network and worsening traffic congestion, the Public Works Department (PWD) has decided to undertake a comprehensive traffic simulation study and road safety audit covering 2,205.68km of roads across its South, North and East zones in Delhi. The ₹ 11.17-crore exercise will use digital models to study traffic movement on individual road stretches and test possible solutions to congestion before implementing them on the ground. The study, which is expected to be completed within three months, will cover 1,796 roads across the three zones. These include 270 roads spanning 426.28 km in the South Zone, 1,137 roads covering 1,374.76 km in the North Zone, and 389 roads stretching across 404.64 km in the East Zone. PWD oversees arterial road networks with width more than 60ft while smaller roads are overseen by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. According to the project report, traffic congestion has been increasing across the city, with even stretches that earlier experienced relatively smooth traffic movement now witnessing frequent bottlenecks, particularly during peak hours. items.text: A View of the Logo of the Election Commission of India at the Nirvachan Sadan. File | Photo Credit: R.V. Moorthy The Election Commission of India (ECI) has separated the Form 6, used for fresh voter registration, and an accompanying declaration in its online version in States where the SIR exercise is underway. Earlier in September, it had already withdrawn the declaration from its digital platforms in States where SIR had been completed. Form 6 is used for fresh voters registrations and since the SIR in Bihar a separate declaration had been added with it in physical forms. However, in the digital mode, it was a single form and this included the declaration. The ECI had justified it saying a single OTP for the two documents had led to suggestions that the form had been tweaked without the approval of the Union Law Ministry. items.headline: RSS to be expanded into 88 regional units: Dattatreya Hosabale
items.blurb: General secretary Dattatreya Hosabale says the organisation has expanded to 103,397 locations nationwide, with a 150% rise in shakhas in West Bengal.
items.text: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) will restructure its organisation into 88 divisions, replacing its existing 46 regional units, as part of its centenary-year expansion plans, general secretary Dattatreya Hosabale said on Wednesday, claiming a 150% increase in shakhas (branches) in West Bengal over the past year. Speaking on the concluding day of the Sangh’s three-day annual meeting at Daly College in Madhya Pradesh’s Indore, Hosabale said the restructuring would help the organisation plan and coordinate its activities more effectively across the country. “Till now, we had 46 prants (regional units). Following organisational elections in November-December, presidents (Sanghchalaks) and new executive bodies will be elected, and 88 sambhags (divisions) will be formed. Future work plans will be prepared from the perspective of these 88 divisions”. Highlighting the organisation’s expansion, Hosabale said the number of shakhas in West Bengal had increased by 150% over the past year. “Earlier, we faced direct and physical opposition while trying to run shakhas there. That opposition is no longer there and the situation has changed,” he said. Referring to violence against RSS workers in the past,

items.headline: 'Policies need to be in tune with reality': Supreme Court calls for fresh look at 2-child norms amid decline in fertility rate
items.blurb: The court cited India's declining fertility rate, which fell to 1.9 in 2024, and warned of the long-term consequences of an ageing population.
items.text: The Supreme Court on Wednesday called for a fresh examination of laws across the country that disqualify people with more than two children from contesting local body elections, holding that the population-control rationale behind such restrictions has “lost their relevance” with India’s fertility rate falling below replacement levels and the country facing the prospect of an ageing population. Emphasising that India must guard against a potentially irreversible decline in fertility and frame policies in tune with changing demographic realities, a bench of justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe referred the matter to a larger bench for reconsideration of a 2003 judgment that upheld the two-child norm . The court observed that the assumptions underlying the earlier ruling in Javed Vs State of Haryana had been overtaken by demographic changes and could no longer be treated as valid. “It would be dangerously complacent to ignore the consequences of India’s changing population growth rate merely because it already has a large population -- the stakes are too high. items.text: Early-stage investor Jungle Ventures is preparing its next cohort of portfolio companies to go public over the coming 18–24 months. A backer of companies such as Livespace, Moglix and Turtlemint, among others, it aims to take two companies public each year, a senior company official said. “The market has changed, and I am fortunate in that sense that in some ways our portfolio is maturing around the same time. For us, the one thing that matters is: can our companies go public? In the spirit of investing behind opportunities, teams that are going to be built to last, a big milestone or validation point is that ability to go public,” said Amit Anand, founding partner and managing director, Jungle Ventures. The firm took fintech company Turtlemint public earlier this year and has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for the public issue of consumer durables maker Atomberg Technologies. “Some of our other companies such as Moglix, Livespace, Citymall, are maturing and could head towards public markets in the near future,” Anand said. items.headline: Interest rates expected to rise for first time in over three years
items.blurb: Most analysts are predicting an increase from 3.75% to 4%, the first increase in more than three years.
items.text: Policymakers at the Bank of England are expected to raise interest rates on Thursday in what would be the first increase to the benchmark rate for more than three years. Most analysts are predicting an rise from 3.75% to 4% in a move that would increase the cost of borrowing for individuals and businesses, but boost savers. The Bank rate has fallen from its 2023–24 peak of 5.25%, although the Bank's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has left the rate unchanged at its last six meetings. Rising inflation, driven primarily by the cost of petrol and diesel, will push policymakers into an interest rate hike, analysts suggest. The announcement will be made by the Bank at 12:00 GMT on Thursday. Close attention will also be paid to any hints from the MPC on the future direction of interest rates. "The decision is increasingly less about whether rates reach 4% and more about what follows after that," said Chris Cheverall, head of UK at trading platform CMC Markets. items.headline: From tunnel boring machines to rockets and pod taxis, L&T explores new manufacturing bets
items.blurb: Larsen and Toubro is exploring at least half a dozen new businesses ranging from nuclear fuel rods and tunnel boring machines to rockets and drones and their components
items.text: MUMBAI: Larsen and Toubro Ltd (L&T) is looking to expand beyond building infrastructure projects and become a bigger manufacturer, exploring at least half a dozen new businesses ranging from nuclear fuel rods and tunnel boring machines to rockets and drones and their components. The move is aimed at diversifying a business still heavily dependent on project execution, as the company approaches ₹ 3 trillion in annual revenue and seeks to sustain growth of 12–15%. The Mumbai-based engineering and construction major is also evaluating opportunities in pod taxis, battery energy storage systems (BESS), traction motors for electric vehicles, and prefabricated residential units, including modular bedrooms and bathrooms that can be installed at construction sites to speed up building, company executives said. These prospective businesses would add to L&T's existing manufacturing portfolio, which spans defence equipment such as howitzers, rocket launchers, warships and the upcoming Zorawar tank, as well as industrial valves, construction equipment and electrolyzers. items.headline: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
items.blurb: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep.
items.text: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents. This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem. Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient. These features are only available with AT&T’s professional $29.99 / month Connected Life monitoring plan. Google’s new overarching approach to AI in K-12 classrooms sounds good on the surface. After consulting educators, researchers, and lawmakers, Google has decided that schools using its education products will be opted out of AI tools by default. It will be up to administrators to manually enable them when these changes roll out in the coming months. When you look at what Google considers to be an AI tool, the nature of the Faustian bargain becomes clear. The affected products are Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search . items.text: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law, hack into unauthorized servers, or release poison gas into major cities and kill us all. Until now, this work has mostly focused on trying to peer into an AI’s “brain” to understand what it is “thinking,” or training models to hew to values that we hold dear. Claude, for instance, has its constitution —a sort of moral code. The trouble is, these techniques don’t seem to work particularly well: Models have been shown to deliberately underperform on tests, hide their intentions , and mislead their evaluators . Now some alignment researchers believe that reverse game theory, also known as mechanism design, might get better results. The cybersecurity agency also said that it has unearthed multiple “individual” cases, where malicious agentic AI systems were exploiting compromised financial systems to undertake unauthorised transactions running into crores of Rupees. items.headline: NPCI Expands Beyond Payments With AI, Blockchain-Focused Subsidiary
items.blurb: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has set up a wholly owned subsidiary, NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd (NTSL), to…
items.text: NPCI has established NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd (NTSL), a wholly owned technology subsidiary, and appointed Vishal Kanvaty its MD & CEO. The new entity will build capabilities beyond NPCI’s core payments mandate, focusing on AI, blockchain, digital financial infrastructure, and global capability centre services. NTSL will also provide technology services for eKYC Setu, the Unified Ticketing Platform, and other digital public infrastructure programmes. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has set up a wholly owned subsidiary, NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd (NTSL), to build capabilities in AI, blockchain, and digital financial infrastructure beyond its core payments mandate. The retail payments operator has appointed Vishal Kanvaty, who has been associated with NPCI for nearly a decade, as the subsidiary’s MD and CEO. NPCI said NTSL will serve as the group’s technology and innovation arm. Its remit will also include global capability centre (GCC) services and technology services for eKYC Setu, the Unified Ticketing Platform (UTP), and other digital public infrastructure (DPI) programmes. According to NPCI, Kanvaty has led the development and commercialisation of several platforms that now fall within NTSL’s focus

items.headline: IndiaAI Mission's three indigenous AI models target offline mobile access, secure use in critical sectors
items.blurb: Three indigenous artificial intelligence (AI) models launched under the Centre's IndiaAI Mission are being developed for applications ranging from offline access on mobile phones to secure use in critical sectors such as defence, cybersecurity and banking.
